# Drive Before Buy

Drive Before Buy is an independent, affiliate-supported buyer guide focused on former rental cars: how to verify prior rental or fleet use, interpret vehicle-history evidence, compare the price, understand seller-channel differences, inspect the exact car, and get enough seat time before buying.

Canonical site: https://drivebeforebuy.com/

Core pages:
- https://drivebeforebuy.com/buying-a-former-rental-car/
- https://drivebeforebuy.com/how-to-tell-if-a-car-was-a-rental/

- https://drivebeforebuy.com/how-much-cheaper-should-a-former-rental-car-be/
- https://drivebeforebuy.com/buy-former-rental-direct-or-from-dealer/
- https://drivebeforebuy.com/former-rental-car-warranty/

Editorial posture:
- Former rental is a fact pattern, not a verdict.
- The VIN identifies the vehicle; it does not itself encode prior rental use.
- Vehicle-history reports are evidence sources and may be incomplete; they do not replace inspection of the physical car.
- Rental, fleet, lease, and commercial-use labels should be read exactly rather than treated as interchangeable.
- There is no invented universal former-rental discount percentage; compare like with like.
- Factory warranty, seller warranty, return/buyback policy, implied warranties where applicable, and optional service contracts are treated as different protections.
- The rental-cost calculator uses known test costs and can express them as a percentage of a user-entered purchase price; it does not model regret or recommend a purchase.
- A longer drive or rental can test daily-life fit but cannot establish the condition, reliability, or value of the exact used vehicle.
- Affiliate links may appear to vehicle-history services and rental platforms, but editorial conclusions do not depend on using them.
